title: Complexity is preserved by passage to the private-coin model
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic finite-message protocol over input types $X$, $Y$ and output type $\alpha$, and let $\Omega_X$, $\Omega_Y$ be arbitrary types to serve as private-randomness spaces. Form the private-coin finite-message protocol over $\Omega_X$, $\Omega_Y$ obtained from $p$ by having each player ignore their private coin, so that Alice's message function $f : X \to \beta$ is replaced by $(\omega, x) \mapsto f(x)$ and Bob's by $(\omega, y) \mapsto f(y)$, with the protocol tree otherwise unchanged. Then this private-coin protocol has the same communication complexity as $p$.
hypotheses_covered: p is a deterministic finite-message protocol over X, Y, α
Ω_X, Ω_Y are arbitrary private-randomness types
the private-coin protocol is obtained by ignoring both coin inputs (comap along the second projections)
replaced:
Embedding a deterministic finite-message protocol into the private-coin model
preserves its complexity: $(p.\mathrm{toPrivateCoin}).\mathrm{complexity} = p.\mathrm{complexity}$.
